Four independent\n * copies of a projection of someone else's table is a drift generator: the next\n * column `liveHolderFragment` starts reading has to be added in four places, and\n * whichever one is missed fails as an entire red suite. Import this instead of\n * adding a fifth.\n *\n * Keep only the columns the fragment reads (`target_owner_id`, `active`,\n * `reschedule_interval_sec`); a fixture that needs the real routines write path\n * should apply the migration instead.\n */\nexport const LIVE_HOLDER_ROUTINES_DDL = `\n  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_shared.routines (\n    id text PRIMARY KEY,\n    target_owner_id text,\n    reschedule_interval_sec integer,\n    active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true\n  )`;\n\n/**\n * EI-6887 — apply ONE real migration SQL file to a hand-provisioned test DB\n * (e.g. `createFreshPgDb` above) via `sql.unsafe`, which speaks SQL, not psql.\n * Newer migrations (461/462/464/465+) carry `\\set ON_ERROR_STOP on` psql\n * meta-commands + a top-level BEGIN;/COMMIT; wrapper per the runner convention\n * — raw `sql.unsafe(readFileSync(file))` on one of these fails TWICE in\n * sequence: first on the `\\`-line (\"syntax error at or near \\\"\\\\\\\"\"), then\n * (once that's stripped) on postgres-js's UNSAFE_TRANSACTION guard (raw txn\n * control isn't allowed on a pooled/non-`sql.begin` client). Older migrations\n * (184/185/189) carry neither, so a test written against them silently\n * doesn't transfer to a newer one. This strips both (the wrapper is a\n * production-apply nicety, not a correctness requirement for a hand-applied\n * single-file DDL run — the file's own DDL is idempotent) so any migration,\n * old or new, applies the same way. That cost 9 red tests across 3 files on 2026-07-27, and the same shape\n * had already burned four separate tickets via `applyPlanItemClaimMigrations`\n * below (EI-9508/9509/9513/9515).\n *\n * `applyMigrationsForTest` applies the list AND proves it is still complete, so\n * the rot fails loudly and names itself instead of surfacing as a column error.\n *\n * ── How completeness is decided (and why not the obvious way) ───────────────\n * Everything is derived FROM THE LIST (plus the explicit `runtimeTables`\n * contract) — there is no second registry to keep in sync, which is what makes\n * this unable to fall behind in turn:\n *   1. parse the listed files for the tables they structurally CREATE/ALTER;\n *   2. scan sql/ for HIGHER-numbered migrations touching those same tables;\n *   3. throw naming the missing file(s) and the table that made each relevant.\n *\n * Two deliberate narrowings, each one a measured counterexample:\n *\n *  - STRUCTURAL statements only (`CREATE TABLE` / `ALTER TABLE`), never a mere\n *    mention. Those are reported separately as advisory context, never as a failure,\n *    UNLESS the migration structurally touches an explicitly declared\n *    `runtimeTables` entry. Runtime tables are a stronger contract: their\n *    creating migration and every later structural migration must be declared,\n *    even when a later migration is wide.\n *\n * A third case the table-overlap heuristic cannot see at all (EI found via\n * WI-35535): a migration can touch ONLY the fixture's declared table by name\n * and still be structurally inapplicable, because it depends on a COLUMN the\n * fixture's deliberately-minimal DDL never built (e.g. an\n * `ADD COLUMN ... The field/\n * op/rank-term vocabulary is closed by the validator, so the compiled SQL is safe; this\n * function does NOT re-validate (the caller — the launch handoff / `set_claim_spec` —\n * validates before persisting the spec on the bee).\n */\nexport async function getNextWorkItem(\n  spec: ClaimSpec,\n  bee: BeeContext,\n  opts: GetNextOpts,\n): Promise<GetNextResult | null> {\n  const sql = opts.client ?? getOrgPg().sql;\n  // WI-5261: prefer the caller's explicitly-resolved workspace (threaded via opts.workspaceId)\n  // over re-deriving it here — activeWorkspaceId() depends on the AsyncLocalStorage request\n  // scope still being intact at this exact point in the async call chain (tool handler ->\n  // getNextForBee -> here -> tier 3's claimNextIssueWorkItem), several awaits deep. Falls back\n  // to the legacy activeWorkspaceId() when omitted (unchanged behavior for other callers).\n  const ws = opts.workspaceId ?? activeWorkspaceId();\n  const resolutionStep = (step: string): number => {\n    const startedAtMs = performance.now();\n    try {\n      opts.onResolutionStep?.(step, { phase: 'start', startedAtMs });\n    } catch {\n      // Observability must not change claim admission or strand a committed row.\n    }\n    return startedAtMs;\n  };\n  const resolutionStepFinished = (step: string, startedAtMs: number): void => {\n    try {\n      opts.onResolutionStep?.(step, {\n        phase: 'end',\n        elapsedMs: Math.max(0, performance.now() - startedAtMs),\n      });\n    } catch {\n      // Observability must not change claim admission or strand a committed row.\n    }\n  };\n  resolutionStep('candidate-ready-flag-read');\n  const useMaintainedReady = await schedulerMaintainedReadyEnabled();\n  resolutionStep('candidate-worker-binding-read');\n  const operationClaims = await import('../blueprint/operation-worker-binding');\n  // This authority read ran on the unbounded shared admin pool BEFORE the ladder's\n  // 15s deadline. A queued read could exhaust the public 30s claim watchdog without\n  // entering any of the bounded feature attempts. Use the caller's dedicated claim\n  // pool and bound acquisition + statements; keep the helper's legacy behavior for\n  // all other claim doors that do not opt into error propagation.\n  const operationClaimRead = await boundedOrgTxn(\n    (tx) => operationClaims.readActiveOperationWorkerClaimBinding(ws, bee.assignee, {\n      sql: tx,\n      throwOnError: true,\n    }),\n    {\n      client: sql,\n      signal: opts.signal,\n      readOnly: true,\n      acquireTimeoutMs: CLAIM_ATTEMPT_BUDGET_MS,\n      statementTimeoutMs: CLAIM_ATTEMPT_BUDGET_MS,\n      lockTimeoutMs: CLAIM_ATTEMPT_BUDGET_MS,\n    },\n  );\n  if (operationClaimRead.status === 'unavailable') {\n    throw new Error(`operation claim authority unavailable: ${operationClaimRead.reason}`);\n  }\n\n  // drain-claim-spec-hardening-2026-07-13 D-002 (fixes EI-11300): `states` is drain-wide\n  // POLICY, so it rides the SPEC — a per-call `opts.states` (the caller's explicit\n  // override) still WINS; only when the caller omits one do we fall back to the spec's\n  // `states` (set once by the fleet leader / queen via scheduler:set_claim_spec, inherited\n  // by every member); neither present ⇒ claimFloorsWhereSql's own `['todo']` default.\n  const effectiveStates = opts.states ?? spec.states;\n  const claimSpecReferencesFleet = claimSpecReferencesField(spec, 'fleet');\n  // EI-21398324268952860: the same authorization read for the GOAL field. A per-goal standing\n  // drain fleet scopes its spec by `{ field:'goal', op:'=', value:<goalId> }` (claim-spec.ts\n  // ITEM_FIELDS `goal`), and its own steward mints plan-stamped work FOR it — which the\n  // plan-lane floor then reserved away from the only fleet entitled to it\n  // (`matchedByFilter=7, claimable=0, planLaneReserved=7`, drain stalled fleet-wide).\n  const claimSpecReferencesGoal = claimSpecReferencesField(spec, 'goal');\n\n  const floorOpts = {\n    harness: opts.harness,\n    workspaceId: ws,\n    states: effectiveStates,\n    swarmId: opts.swarmId,\n    excludeRedundant: opts.excludeRedundant,\n    useMaintainedReady,\n    // Release-cooldown floor (P-005 / EI-6956): a row THIS bee just released is\n    // excluded for it (and only it) for the cooldown window — no claim/release\n    // ping-pong under a stable rank.\n    cooldownAssignee: bee.assignee,\n    // EI-14806: the cross-machine-rig floor now applies to the FEATURE family too (tiers 1/2\n    // query this fragment). Omitted/false ⇒ a payload.needs_2_machine_rig feature is excluded\n    // for a single-box caller, matching the issue-family tier-3 floor (claimNextIssueWorkItem).\n    rigAvailable: opts.rigAvailable,\n    claimantFleetSlug: opts.fleetSlug,\n    claimSpecReferencesFleet,\n    claimSpecReferencesGoal,\n  };\n\n  // EI-18805386252364731: the claim query runs on the `harness_admin` pool, which carries a\n  // role-default lock_timeout but DELIBERATELY NO statement_timeout (migrations share it and\n  // must run unbounded). An over-cost claim spec therefore did not fail — it HUNG, until the\n  // MCP client transport gave up minutes later, and a JS-side AbortController cannot rescue it\n  // because postgres-js does not cancel an in-flight query. The member then reads a pull that\n  // never returned as \"the lane is drained\" and parks, while the lane is in fact full.\n  //\n  // So every attempt runs inside a BOUNDED txn, and the whole ladder shares ONE budget: a spec\n  // too expensive to decide now surfaces as a typed OrgTxnTimeoutError the tool reports, never\n  // as a drain-shaped `null`. {"timestamp":"2026-10-10T04:34:47.607Z","ordinal":122,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a12411-e413-7d30-ae42-79e0a4cd8440","turn_id":"01a12412-9b14-79b2-a098-a1990e4bc82d","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-02015053-40a0-4b80-9650-7c7515bf2baf","process_id":"10596","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '1,220p' packages/operator-core/lib/pg-bounded-txn.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '1,220p' packages/operator-core/lib/pg-bounded-txn.ts","name":"pg-bounded-txn.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/pg-bounded-txn.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"/**\n * pg-bounded-txn — a bounded transaction on the operator admin pool.\n *\n * WHY (reliability): getOrgPg() (the `harness_admin` pool) carries a role-default\n * `lock_timeout` (15s) + `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` (60s) but DELIBERATELY\n * NO `statement_timeout` — migrations + long maintenance tooling run on this same\n * pool and must be allowed to run unbounded. The cost of that omission: an\n * INTERACTIVE write tool that runs raw queries on this pool (e.g. work_items:comment\n * → commentIssue → getOrCreateThread/addPost) has NO per-statement bound. A query\n * that stalls for any NON-lock reason — a CPU-starved backend, a slow scan, a buffer\n * wait — runs UNBOUNDED and HANGS the MCP call until the client transport gives up.\n *\n * Crucially, a JS-level watchdog cannot rescue it: postgres-js does NOT cancel an\n * in-flight query when an AbortController fires, so the route-stack 30s abort only\n * yields a 408 once the handler finally returns. The ONLY thing that actually\n * unblocks a wedged query is a DB-side statement_timeout. (Root cause of the\n * reported \"work_items:comment hung, then timed out on a bounded retry.\")\n *\n * boundedOrgTxn wraps admin-pool work in ONE transaction with a\n * SET LOCAL statement_timeout + lock_timeout, so the work is:\n *   - ATOMIC  — partial writes can't half-land and a post-stall retry can't\n *               duplicate (every statement commits together or not at all); and\n *   - BOUNDED — a stall surfaces as a fast, typed OrgTxnTimeoutError (mapped from\n *               PG 57014 statement_timeout / 55P03 lock_timeout) that the caller\n *               turns into a clean { ok:false, error } result (runBulk does this\n *               for the bulk tools), instead of an indefinite hang.\n *\n * It is the interactive transaction counterpart to pg-read-query's bounded READ ONLY txn,\n * and a deliberately lighter sibling of locks/inWorkspaceTxn: NO per-workspace\n * advisory lock (a coordination append must not serialize the entire workspace).\n * Migrations + long tooling keep calling getOrgPg() directly and stay unbounded.\n */\n\nimport {\n  DEFAULT_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS,\n  DbCallDeadlineError,\n  getOrgPg,\n  retryOnRetryableDbDeadline,\n  withAcquisitionDeadline,\n} from '@papercusp/db-org';\n\n/** The postgres-js client type the org handle exposes (same alias pg-read-query uses). */\ntype OrgSql = ReturnType<typeof getOrgPg>['sql'];\n\ntype CancelableQuery = {\n  cancel?: () => void | Promise<unknown>;\n  /** postgres.js Query objects expose these; test doubles may omit them. */\n  executed?: boolean;\n  active?: boolean;\n  catch?: (onRejected: (reason: unknown) => void) => Promise<unknown>;\n};\n\n/**\n * Wrap a postgres-js transaction client so an abandoned caller can cancel every\n * query it has started. `withBoundedTimeout` deliberately races the caller's\n * promise instead of awaiting it after the deadline; without this bridge the\n * transaction would keep its connection busy until PostgreSQL eventually\n * finished it (EI-23070293747146376).\n */\nfunction cancellableTransaction(\n  tx: OrgSql,\n  signal?: AbortSignal,\n): {\n  tx: OrgSql;\n  assertNotAborted: () => void;\n  abort: Promise<never> | undefined;\n  cleanup: () => void;\n} {\n  if (!signal) {\n    return { tx, assertNotAborted: () => undefined, abort: undefined, cleanup: () => undefined };\n  }\n\n  const active = new Set<CancelableQuery>();\n  let cancelled = signal.aborted;\n  let removeAbortListener: (() => void) | undefined;\n  const abortReason = () => signal.reason ?? Object.assign(new Error('boundedOrgTxn aborted'), { name: 'AbortError' });\n  const cancelQuery = (query: CancelableQuery) => {\n    // postgres.js returns a lazy Query for BOTH executable statements and SQL\n    // fragments. Cancelling an unexecuted fragment rejects its own promise with\n    // 57014 even though nobody awaited it; that unhandled rejection killed the\n    // operator host. A completed query also has nothing left to cancel.\n    if (query.executed === false || query.active === false) return;\n    try {\n      // Query.cancel() returns void: it is the original Query promise, not the\n      // return value of cancel(), that rejects when PostgreSQL acknowledges the\n      // cancellation. Observe it before sending the cancellation request.\n      void query.catch?.(() => undefined);\n      void Promise.resolve(query.cancel?.()).catch(() => undefined);\n    } catch {\n      // Cancellation is best-effort; the original abort/error remains authoritative.\n    }\n  };\n  const cancelActive = () => {\n    cancelled = true;\n    for (const query of active) {\n      cancelQuery(query);\n    }\n  };\n  const assertNotAborted = () => {\n    if (cancelled || signal.aborted) throw abortReason();\n  };\n  const track = <T>(query: T): T => {\n    const candidate = query as T & CancelableQuery;\n    if (!candidate || typeof candidate.cancel !== 'function') return query;\n    // postgres.js uses the same thenable Query object for a top-level query and\n    // for a SQL fragment. Assimilating it here with Promise.resolve(query)\n    // executes a fragment as a standalone statement. That produced parser\n    // errors such as `syntax error at or near \"last_released_by\"` from the\n    // scheduler's release-floor fragment. Keep the object in the cancellation\n    // set without observing its then/finally methods; postgres.js will execute\n    // it only when the caller awaits the completed outer query.\n    active.add(candidate);\n    if (cancelled) {\n      cancelQuery(candidate);\n    }\n    return query;\n  };\n  const invoke = (...args: unknown[]) => {\n    assertNotAborted();\n    return track(Reflect.apply(tx as unknown as (...input: unknown[]) => unknown, tx, args));\n  };\n  const wrapped = Object.assign(invoke, tx) as unknown as OrgSql;\n  const unsafe = (tx as unknown as { unsafe?: (...args: unknown[]) => unknown }).unsafe;\n  if (unsafe) {\n    Object.defineProperty(wrapped, 'unsafe', {\n      configurable: true,\n      value: (...args: unknown[]) => {\n        assertNotAborted();\n        return track(Reflect.apply(unsafe, tx, args));\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  const abort = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {\n    const onAbort = () => {\n      cancelActive();\n      reject(abortReason());\n    };\n    if (signal.aborted) onAbort();\n    else {\n      signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });\n      removeAbortListener = () => signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);\n    }\n  });\n  // A pre-aborted signal rejects `abort` synchronously, while the transaction\n  // callback still throws from `assertNotAborted()` before it reaches the\n  // Promise.race below. Observe the promise now so that early assertion errors\n  // cannot leave this sibling rejection unhandled; the original rejected\n  // promise remains the one raced when the callback reaches that path.\n  void abort.catch(() => undefined);\n  return {\n    tx: wrapped,\n    assertNotAborted,\n    abort,\n    cleanup: () => {\n      removeAbortListener?.();\n      active.clear();\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Thrown when a bounded admin-pool txn can't finish in time: a statement exceeds\n * `statement_timeout` (PG `57014`) or a lock wait exceeds `lock_timeout` (PG `55P03`).\n * Callers map this to a structured busy result instead of leaking a raw postgres\n * error. The originating PG error is preserved on `.cause` / `.pgCode`.\n *\n * EI-19404770733829453: a bare \"canceling statement due to lock timeout\" names no\n * cause, so every caller who hits it either retries blindly or goes hand-querying\n * `pg_stat_activity`. When `blockerHint` is available (best-effort — see\n * `describeContentionAtFailure` below), it is folded into `.message` so the error\n * ITSELF says what blocked it (e.g. a long-running migration holding a table lock)\n * instead of leaving that diagnosis to whoever reads the stack trace next.\n */\nexport class OrgTxnTimeoutError extends Error {\n  readonly pgCode: string;\n  readonly blockerHint?: string;\n  /**\n   * EI-21831306274538775 — did PostgreSQL actually raise this SQLSTATE (`'pg'`), or did a\n   * caller SYNTHESIZE the same typed error to report exhausting its own wall-clock budget\n   * (`'caller-budget'`)?\n   *\n   * Callers deliberately synthesize a 57014 so an expired budget cannot be mistaken for\n   * \"nothing matched\" — correct, but it left the two causes INDISTINGUISHABLE downstream\n   * while the message asserted \"the database stalled\", which for a synthesized one is\n   * simply untrue. Measured cost: `scheduler:get_next`'s claim ladder raises exactly this,\n   * and the resulting `pgCode: '57014'` was reported twice as reproduced PostgreSQL\n   * contention — sending triage to the connection pool for a budget that ran out inside the\n   * scheduler. A retryable-timeout contract for the caller does not require lying about\n   * which clock expired.\n   *\n   * Defaults to `'pg'` so every existing raise site keeps its meaning; only a caller that\n   * knows it is synthesizing passes `'caller-budget'`.\n   */\n  readonly timeoutSource: 'pg' | 'caller-budget';\n  constructor(\n    pgCode: string,\n    cause: unknown,\n    blockerHint?: string,\n    timeoutSource: 'pg' | 'caller-budget' = 'pg',\n    operation: 'read' | 'write' = 'write',\n  ) {\n    const subject = operation === 'read' ? 'operator read query' : 'operator write';\n    const base =\n      timeoutSource === 'caller-budget'\n        ? `${subject} was abandoned after exceeding the CALLER's own time budget (reported as pg ${pgCode} so it is never mistaken for \"nothing matched\"; PostgreSQL itself did not time out) — retry shortly`\n        : pgCode === '55P03'\n          ? `${subject} timed out waiting for a row/advisory lock (pg 55P03 lock_timeout) — retry shortly`\n          : `${subject} exceeded its time budget (pg 57014 statement_timeout) — the database stalled; retry shortly`;\n    super(blockerHint ? `${base} — ${blockerHint}` : base);\n    this.name = 'OrgTxnTimeoutError';\n    this.pgCode = pgCode;\n    this.cause = cause;\n    this.blockerHint = blockerHint;\n    this.timeoutSource = timeoutSource;\n  }\n}\n\n/** PG SQLSTATEs that mean \"couldn't finish in time\": statement_timeout + lock_timeout. */\nconst CONTENTION_CODES = new Set(['57014', '55P03']);\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":23766}},"started_at_ms":1791606887607,"completed_at_ms":1791606887607}}
{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T04:34:47.756Z","ordinal":123,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a12411-e413-7d30-ae42-79e0a4cd8440","turn_id":"01a12412-9b14-79b2-a098-a1990e4bc82d","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-43ace075-98ea-45bd-b8ee-5659da2076eb","process_id":"45281","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '8688,8835p' packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '8688,8835p' packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts","name":"work-items.ts","path":"packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"export async function claimNextIssueWorkItem(\n  filter: ClaimNextFilter,\n  explicitActiveWorkspaceId: string,\n  opts: {\n    /** Optional caller-owned client; scheduler:get_next uses its isolated claim pool. */\n    client?: OrgSql;\n    /** Reuse the scheduler's bounded authority read across candidate families. */\n    operationClaimRead?: ActiveOperationWorkerClaimRead;\n    issueKinds?: readonly IssueStoreKind[];\n    ids?: readonly string[];\n    /** WI-5258: ids the caller's spec NEGATIVELY excludes (e.g. `not:{id in [...]}` —\n     *  \"already handled, skip these\") — extracted by get-next.ts's tier 3 caller.\n     *  Without this, a fleet leader's exclusion clause silently vanished the moment\n     *  tier 1/2 missed and tier 3 took over: claimNextIssueWorkItem previously had no\n     *  way to see it, so the very ids a spec meant to skip came right back through the\n     *  fallback. Undefined/empty ⇒ no exclusion, unchanged behavior. */\n    excludeIds?: readonly string[];\n    /** The caller's FULL claim-spec filter, already compiled to a SQL fragment by\n     *  get-next.ts's `compileFilter` (passed DOWN rather than imported, so this module\n     *  keeps its existing get-next → work-items import direction and no cycle forms).\n     *\n     *  Why this exists: `issueKinds`/`ids`/`excludeIds` above can only express the kind\n     *  and id legs of a spec. Every OTHER leg — `paths` globs, `plan`, `title`, `tags`,\n     *  and any `any`/`not` combination of them — used to be invisible to this claim\n     *  query, so tier 3 would atomically claim a row the spec never admitted and rely on\n     *  claim-spec-store.ts's post-claim `matchesWorkItemClaimSpec` re-check to release it\n     *  and retry. That retry shares MAX_PLAN_LANE_ATTEMPTS (5), a budget whose own comment\n     *  sizes it for a DIFFERENT failure mode (consecutive plan-lane-BLOCKED candidates).\n     *  For a narrow fleet lane that budget is nowhere near enough: measured on\n     *  p2p-release-lane@9, 26 of 1073 lane-wide claimable rows matched the spec (2.4%), so\n     *  P(>=1 match in 5 draws) ~ 11.6% — i.e. ~88% of scheduler:get_next pulls returned a\n     *  FALSE \"no claimable work\", indistinguishable from a genuinely drained lane. Three\n     *  separate fleet members independently misreported that as \"floor-gated\" while\n     *  work_items:claimable (which DOES compile the full filter, via\n     *  issueClaimCandidateSubquery) correctly reported 26 claimable.\n     *\n     *  Threading the compiled filter here makes the claim path select a SPEC-MATCHING row\n     *  atomically on the first attempt, which re-unifies claim with read and removes the\n     *  quarantine claim-then-release round-trip for ALL spec shapes (that dance also caused\n     *  the EI-15019 / EI-14837 spurious-wake incidents). claimFloorsWhereSql(tx, {\n            harness: filter.harness,\n            workspaceId: explicitActiveWorkspaceId,\n            states: filter.states,\n            swarmId: filter.swarmId,\n            excludeRedundant: filter.excludeRedundant,\n            useMaintainedReady: opts.priorityBeforeFeature.useMaintainedReady,\n            cooldownAssignee: filter.assignee,\n            rigAvailable: filter.rigAvailable,\n            claimantFleetSlug: filter.claimantFleetSlug,\n            claimSpecReferencesFleet: filter.claimSpecReferencesFleet,\n            claimSpecReferencesGoal: filter.claimSpecReferencesGoal,\n          })\n        : tx`TRUE`;\n      const rows = await measureResolutionStep('candidate-issue-claim-update', () => tx<FeatureRowDb[]>`\n    UPDATE harness_shared.work_items AS target\n       SET payload = jsonb_set(\n             COALESCE(target.payload, '{}'::jsonb),\n             '{claim_history_post_id}',\n             to_jsonb(COALESCE((\n               SELECT max(post.id)\n                 FROM harness_shared.coord_thread_posts post\n                WHERE post.workspace_id = ${issueWs}\n             ), 0)),\n             true\n           ),\n           taken_by = ${filter.assignee}, taken_at = now(), last_progress_at = NULL, updated_ts = ${Date.now()}\n     WHERE (workspace_id, harness_slug, feature_id) = (\n       SELECT workspace_id, harness_slug, feature_id\n         FROM harness_shared.work_items wi\n        WHERE wi.item_kind = ANY(${issueKinds}::text[])\n          AND wi.workspace_id = ${issueWs}\n          AND ${selection.where}\n          AND ${operationClaims.operationWorkerClaimWhereSql(tx, operationClaimRead, {\n            payload: 'wi.payload', id: 'wi.feature_id', harness: 'wi.harness_slug',\n          })}\n          -- WI-4309: narrow to the spec's closed-world id set, when one was extracted.\n          AND ${idFilter ? rigAvailable: args.rigAvailable,\n          ignoreStoredSpec: !specOn && !reconciliation.scope,\n          // P-006 (fleet-leader-frictions-six-improvements-2026-07-10, WI-3763): this is\n          // void backfillToolInvocationMetadataByCallId({\n                workspaceId: ident.workspaceId,\n                toolName: 'scheduler:get_next',\n                dispatchCallId: Source-only inspection at staging HEAD 238f94b916 (the inspected files match HEAD) found: packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/get-next.integration.test.ts already uses createFreshPgDb('sched-get-next'), injects db.sql through getNextWorkItem's client option, seeds issue/feature rows, and exercises the priority preclaim. FreshPgDb is a throwaway database with a max-4 postgres-js pool and an execution-level debug hook. getNextWorkItem forwards its client and AbortSignal into claimNextIssueWorkItem; that path measures candidate-issue-claim-transaction, candidate-issue-claim-update, and candidate-issue-post-claim-reread separately. boundedOrgTxn wraps sql.begin/setup with the 45s default acquisition deadline; its cancellation wrapper is installed only after the begin callback is entered.\",\n  left: \"No code changes, tests, or runtime experiments were made; no shared scheduler call was retried. The Oct 7 timeout's inner DB phase remains unknown. Live loop status was active at 60s but rewakeGuaranteed=false (last-fire-no-loop-turn); this is recorded as a continuation risk, with cause not yet diagnosed.\",\n  insight: \"A safe discriminator can use the existing FreshPgDb path plus getNextWorkItem({client, signal}) on a one-slot isolated pool. At candidate-issue-claim-transaction start, a test-only held transaction can occupy that pool before the scheduler's next begin. Abort the supplied signal while held, verify no candidate-issue-claim-update/post-claim-reread event or claim SQL occurs until release, then release and verify the pre-aborted transaction exits without claiming. A shorter acquisition deadline can be set via PAPERCUSP_DB_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS before module import; this tests cancellation ordering without waiting 45s. This demonstrates the acquisition-wait mechanism only and does not attribute the historical incident.\",\n  next: \"Send the exact isolated-test design to the current fleet leader and request explicit authorization before adding/running the test. Continue to avoid the shared scheduler.\",\n  checks: [\n    {\n      id: \"issue-preclaim-budget-order\",\n      claim: \"Priority issue preclaim runs before the claim-ladder remaining-budget guard.\",\n      recheck: \"Read get-next.ts around the priority preclaim and attempt().\",\n      falsifier: \"The ladder budget check executes before entering claimIssue(true).\",\n      verified: \"At staging HEAD 238f94b916, the priority block calls claimIssue(true) before feature attempts; attempt() checks ladderDeadline immediately before boundedOrgTxn. @2026-10-10T04:37:42Z\"\n    },\n    {\n      id: \"issue-claim-acquire-vs-30s-phase\",\n      claim: \"The issue preclaim passes client and signal without an acquisition override; boundedOrgTxn uses a 45s default and attaches cancellation after begin callback entry.\",\n      recheck: \"Read get-next.ts, work-items.ts claimNextIssueWorkItem, pg-bounded-txn.ts, and db connection.ts.\",\n      falsifier: \"The issue preclaim supplies acquireTimeoutMs <= 30s, or the default is <= 30s, or signal cancellation wraps sql.begin before pool checkout.\",\n      verified: \"At staging HEAD 238f94b916, claimNextIssueWorkItem receives {client,signal}; boundedOrgTxn defaults to DEFAULT_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS=45,000ms (PAPERCUSP_DB_TX_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_MS override), and creates cancellableTransaction only inside the sql.begin callback. @2026-10-10T04:37:42Z\"\n    },\n    {\n      id: \"freshpg-client-injection\",\n      claim: \"The registered FreshPgDb integration fixture exposes a safe isolated database and a client-injection seam for the scheduler call.\",\n      recheck: \"Read get-next.integration.test.ts setup, createFreshPgDb, and GetNextWorkItem options.\",\n      falsifier: \"The fixture uses shared production data or getNextWorkItem cannot accept a caller-owned client.\",\n      verified: \"get-next.integration.test.ts uses createFreshPgDb('sched-get-next') and sets getOrgPg to that fixture client; getNextWorkItem accepts opts.client, which it forwards to issue-claim transactions. The fixture creates a throwaway DB and max-4 client. @2026-10-10T04:37:42Z\"\n    }\n  ]\n};\nconst r = await invoke({ name: \"work_items:checkpoint\", args });\nconst raw = r?.content?.map(c => c.type === \"text\" ? c.text : \"\").join(\"\\n\") || JSON.stringify(r);\ntext(raw.slice(0, 7500));\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12412-9b14-79b2-a098-a1990e4bc82d","create_time":1791607187.8821435}}}
